html:
The Kamëntšá are an Indigenous people of the Sibundoy Valley in Putumayo, southern Colombia, a high valley where the Andes drop toward the Amazon.

Their language is an isolate, unrelated to any other. They share the valley with the Inga, who speak a form of Quechua. Sibundoy healers are known across the region for their knowledge of plants, including the brew yagé. Each year before Lent they hold the Bëtscnaté, a festival of reconciliation and plenty. Capuchin missionaries ran the valley from the late 1800s into the 1900s and took much of the land for settlers. The Quillacinga lived to the west.
